approachQuestion.prompt:
Install spaced beacons

Given n distinct integer candidate coordinates and k beacons, choose k coordinates maximizing the minimum distance between consecutive chosen coordinates after sorting. Input may be reordered. 2<=k<=n<=200000; coordinates in [0,10^9]. Examples: [0,3,4,10], k=3 -> 4 using 0,4,10; [2,9], k=2 -> 7. Prefer scalable worst-case time, then memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Heapsort coordinates in place. Binary-search a proposed minimum distance d; greedily place a beacon at the first coordinate and then at the earliest coordinate at least d after the last placement. Retain the largest d permitting at least k placements.
options.feedback: Earliest feasible placement leaves maximal room for later beacons; feasibility is true below a distance boundary, so search for the last feasible value.

options.text: Sort a copy and perform the same greedy feasibility search.
options.feedback: The answer is correct, but the copy adds avoidable storage because reordering the input is permitted.

options.text: Choose the first k sorted coordinates and return their smallest gap.
options.feedback: For [0,3,4,10], k=3, the first three yield 1 whereas choosing 0,4,10 yields 4.

For a fixed spacing, placing the next beacon at the earliest feasible coordinate leaves maximal room for later placements. Larger spacing only reduces feasibility, so retain the last feasible distance, not the first.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. D is coordinate range. Include in-place iterative heapsort and full greedy scans in iterative binary search. All operations are fixed-width constant time; no recursion or copies. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

options.text: O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sort coordinates, then run a linear placement test per distance midpoint.
details: Sorting costs O(n log n), then O(log(D+2)) candidate spacings each require an O(n) greedy placement scan. Add these phases. Both heapsort and search are iterative and reuse the input, leaving O(1) auxiliary space.

“O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Earliest feasible placement leaves maximal room for later beacons; feasibility is true below a distance boundary, so search for the last feasible value.
“O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space”: Both heapsort and feasibility checks are iterative over the supplied array, so no coordinate copy or recursive stack grows with n.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Sorting coordinates and repeatedly checking a spacing threshold cannot be constant work as n grows.
